ORAL JUDGMENT
With consent of learned counsel for parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. Heard Sri Anjaneya M. and Sri MK Soudagar, learned counsel for parties.
3.
Challenging judgment and award dated 11.09.2017 passed in MVC no.1361/2015 by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Ranebennur1, these appeals are filed.
4. MFA no.101855/2018 is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation and MFA no.100365/2018 is filed by NWKRTC challenging award on negligence.
5. Sri Anjaneya M, learned counsel for appellant in claimant's appeal submitted that on 21.03.2015 claimant was travelling in Bus no.KA-42/F-1199 belonging to NWKRTC from Honnali to Haveri.
En route, it collided with a For short, 'Tribunal' NC: 2026:KHC-D:3478 HC-KAR motorcycle and thereafter, dashed against a bridge.

In accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite treatment at Government Hospital, Honnali and at OM Hospital, Ranebennur, he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against NWKRTC was filed.
6. On contest wherein claim petition was opposed on all counts, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant and Dr.Manoj deposed as PW1 and PW2 respectively and got marked documents at Exs.P1 to P15.
Official of Insurer was examined as RW1 and did not mark any document.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus and claimant was entitled for compensation as follows:

11. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused impugned judgment and award and certified copy of deposition made available by learned counsel for claimant/appellant.

sentences.text:
From above, since both claimant as well as Corporation are assailing award on quantum and finding on negligence, points that would arise for consideration are:
1) Whether Tribunal was justified in fixing entire negligence on bus driver?
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3478 HC-KAR 2) Whether assessment on compensation by Tribunal calls for modification as prayed?

Point no.1:
13.
Admittedly, claimant herein was inmate of bus.
Even if, accident occurred due to contributory negligence of motorcycle involved in accident, claimant would be entitled for claim against any one of tortfeasors.
Besides, prosecution records produced at Ex.P1 to P4 would arraign only bus driver.

Therefore,
challenge on negligence by Corporation would be untenable.
Point no.1 is answered in affirmative.

Point no.2:
14.
On quantum, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.300/- per day i.e., Rs.9,000/- per month, same was not substantiated with any specific material.
Tribunal has taken notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month.

But, notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- per month, therefore,
Tribunal was not justified in taking it at Rs.7,000/-.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3478 HC-KAR 15.

Thus compensation towards future loss of income would be Rs.8,000 X 3% X 12 X 17 =
Rs.48,960/-
16.
Indeed, PW2-doctor assessed 25% disability caused due to fracture of right patella in Ex.P10-disability certificate.
However, perusal of deposition as well as Ex.P10
would not reveal any restriction in movement of knee joint on account of malunion of fracture.
Normally, fracture of patella would not cause disability.
17. Therefore, assessment of loss of earning capacity at 3% by Tribunal would not appear either contrary to record or grossly inadequate and is confirmed.
However, claimant sustained fracture.
Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering, which would appear inadequate and is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
18. Tribunal has awarded Rs.9,600/- towards medical expenses, Rs.1,000/- towards attendant charges, Rs.1,000/- towards conveyance charges and Rs.2,000/- towards Food, Die, extra nourishment charges.
Considering NC: 2026:KHC-D:3478 HC-KAR medical bills, treatment records, same would just and proper and are confirmed.

sentences.text: Fracture of Patella would take about two months to heal.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled to sum of Rs.16,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
20. Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Though, fracture of patella may not have caused any disability, PW2 has noted that same was causing discomfort.

Therefore,
compensation towards loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.

21. Thus, total compensation would be at Rs.1,23,560/-.
22.

Insofar as award of interest, Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd.
v. Mannat Johal2, has held rate of interest to be awarded in motor accident claims is to be at 7.5%.

Accordingly, point no.2 is answered as partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. MFA no.101855/2018 is allowed in part.

ii. Appellant/claimant is entitled to receive Rs.1,23,560/- as against Rs.75,440/-
awarded by Tribunal with interest at rate of 7% p.a., from date of petition till realization.
iii. Respondent-NWKRTC is directed to deposit enhanced compensation before Tribunal within a period of eight (8) weeks from date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
iv. On deposit, Tribunal is directed to release entire compensation amount in favour of claimant.
v. MFA No.100365/2018 is dismissed.
